title: Event Handling in React
summary: Shows how to attach event handlers to JSX elements (onClick, onMouseOver, onMouseOut), update state from them with useState, and combine that with inline styles and a ternary to build a button that turns black on hover and white when the mouse leaves.

concepts.heading: Attaching handlers in JSX
points: HTML event attributes become camelCase props in JSX: onclick becomes onClick, onmouseover becomes onMouseOver, onmouseout becomes onMouseOut.

The value is a JavaScript expression in curly braces that references a function: onClick={handleClick}. Pass the function itself, not a call (handleClick without parentheses), so React runs it when the event fires rather than at render.
A first test handler that only logs to the console proves the wiring; it fires each time the event occurs.
W3Schools' HTML event attributes list is a handy catalogue of other events to react to; remember to camelCase the name in JSX.
(Extra) React passes every handler a synthetic event object as its first argument (handleClick(event)); this lecture does not need it, the forms lecture uses event.target.value.

(Extra) onMouseOver/onMouseOut also fire when the pointer moves between child elements inside the target; onMouseEnter/onMouseLeave fire only once on entering and leaving, which is often what a hover effect wants.

concepts.heading: Changing what is rendered from an event
points: Heading text that must change is stored in state: const [headingText, setHeadingText] = useState("Hello"). The name pair (value, setValue) is the usual convention.
In the handler call setHeadingText("Submitted"). React re-renders the component and the h1 {headingText} shows the new value.
useState has to be imported from react before use: import React, { useState } from "react"; (or just import { useState } from "react" with the newer JSX transform used by Vite).
The argument to useState is the initial value used on first render only.

concepts.heading: Hover colour change: state + inline style + ternary
points: Inline style in JSX takes an object with camelCase keys inside double braces: style={{ backgroundColor: "black" }} (outer braces for the JS expression, inner for the object).
A second state value tracks hover: const [isMouseOver, setMouseOver] = useState(false). It starts false because the pointer is not over the button on load.
handleMouseOver calls setMouseOver(true); handleMouseOut calls setMouseOver(false).
The style picks its colour with a ternary: backgroundColor: isMouseOver ? "black" : "white". Every state change triggers a re-render that recomputes this.
Without onMouseOut the button would turn black and never revert; both events are needed.
This brings together conditional rendering, inline styling, event props and state.
(Extra) The setter name setMouseOver does not have to mirror the state name exactly (isMouseOver); only the [value, setter] order from useState matters.

concepts.heading: What comes next
points: The following lecture uses the same input element to handle form events, so the input here is just a placeholder for now.

task.name: Hover-to-black button
task.starting_point: CodeSandbox starter: App with an h1 saying Hello, a text input with a name placeholder and a Submit button.
task.goal: On clicking Submit the heading changes to Submitted; hovering the button turns its background black and leaving turns it white again.
steps: Add onClick={handleClick} to the button; first just console.log in it to check wiring.
Create headingText state (initial "Hello"), render it in the h1 and make handleClick call setHeadingText("Submitted").
Add onMouseOver with handleMouseOver; log to confirm it fires on entering the button.
Create isMouseOver state (initial false); handleMouseOver sets it to true.
Apply style={{ backgroundColor: isMouseOver ? "black" : "white" }} to the button.
Add onMouseOut with handleMouseOut that sets isMouseOver back to false.
task.expected_result: White button turns black under the cursor, back to white when the cursor leaves; clicking changes the heading to Submitted.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 36 - React.js/36.33 Event Handling in React/event-handling-in-react/src/App.jsx

pitfalls: Writing onClick={handleClick()} calls the function during render instead of on click.
Using lowercase attribute names (onclick, onmouseover) instead of camelCase.
Forgetting the double braces for the inline style object.
Misspelling the event name (onMouseOut) so the revert never fires.
(Extra) For plain colour-on-hover, CSS :hover would be simpler; this exercise is about practising state and events.

gaps_and_ideas: New 'React events' lesson (blurb: attach camelCase event props such as onClick and onMouseOver to JSX, and use state set inside handlers to change what renders). Tasks: (1) log a message on click, (2) change the heading to Submitted with useState, (3) black-on-hover button with onMouseOver/onMouseOut, a boolean state and a ternary inside style={{ }}, (4) add onDoubleClick to reset the heading, (5) show a counter of how many times the button was hovered.
Starter code idea: App with an h1 'Hello', a text input and a white Submit button, plus empty handleClick / handleMouseOver / handleMouseOut functions to fill in.

Demo idea: an event log panel beside the button that appends each event name as it fires (mouseover, mouseout, click), with a toggle to compare onMouseOver vs onMouseEnter when the button contains a child span.
